# NextGenRedTeam Threat Lab Blog

> High-fidelity threat emulation research, hardware reverse engineering, and offensive AI orchestration.

## Active Research Threads

- [Experimental Rebuild Tuning: llama.cpp MoE Memory Gains and Dense Regressions](/blog/experimental-rebuild-tuning-llama-cpp-moe-vs-dense.html): We compiled and tested a custom llama.cpp fork on our RTX node. Here is how it optimized Mixture of Experts (MoE) memory, why it fumbled dense model speeds, and why we rolled back.
- [Building a Private AI Research Lab: Bridging LiteLLM and SearXNG on NextGenPVE](/blog/building-private-ai-research-lab-searxng-litellm.html): How we containerized and bridged SearXNG and LiteLLM in LXC 205 on NextGenPVE for privacy-respecting threat intelligence gathering and local AI orchestration.
- [Deep Benchmarks v7: Pushing NextGenPVE to the Limit](/blog/deep-benchmarks-v7.html): Reviewing the latest local LLM benchmarks across NextGenPVE-RTX and the new NextGenPVE-NPU hardware.
- [Massive Environment Overhaul: Brain-RTX Hyper-Optimization & Benchmark Results](/blog/massive-environment-overhaul-brain-rtx.html): How I heavily modified the GPU daemon on my local rig to handle massive 12k+ token agentic context windows without choking.
- [The NPU Journey Part 4: Conquering the Final Boss (Strict JSONs, CMM Boot Windows, and Gateways)](/blog/npu-journey-part-4-the-final-boss.html): Resolving strict post_config type checks, handling the 65-second CMM boot window, and building a LiteLLM translation layer for unified edge NPU inference.
- [The NPU Journey Part 3: Night Shift Compilation Breakthroughs (AppArmor, LXC Ghost Memory)](/blog/npu-journey-part-3-compilation-breakthroughs.html): Resolving nested container virtualization blocks, bypassing AppArmor security confinement, and clearing ghost memory traps during our high-throughput compilation sprint on the AX8850.
- [The NPU Journey Part 2: The True Guide to Deploying LLMs on the Axera AX8850](/blog/npu-journey-part-2-deploying-llms.html): The definitive, step-by-step technical guide to native LLM deployment on the AX8850 NPU via PCIe passthrough inside an unprivileged LXC container.
- [The NPU Journey Part 1: Taming the Axera AX8850 (And Why We Reverse-Engineered Everything for Nothing)](/blog/npu-journey-part-1-taming-axera-ax8850.html): Admitting our over-engineering mistakes: how broken vendor paths and JSON parser bugs led us to reverse engineer everything for nothing, and the reality of taming the Axera AX8850 NPU.
- [ReThink: Bypassing DKMS and Virtualizing the AX8850 NPU in NextGenPVE LXC](/blog/rethinking-npu-virtualization-nextgenpve-lxc.html): How we decoupled the Axera AX8850 NPU from bare-metal, resolved NextGenPVE LXC DKMS compiler conflicts, and cleared stale CMM allocations to host localized reasoning LLMs.
- [Ultimate Guide: Zero-Copy Inference on the AX8850 NPU](/blog/ultimate-guide-zero-copy-ax8850.html): How to bypass Radxa's Python CPU bottlenecks, compile a native C++ OpenAI server, and achieve stable zero-copy inference on the AX8850 NPU.
- [Conquering the Silicon: Building a Custom 'Ollama' Orchestrator for the AX8850 NPU (Part II)](/blog/conquering-silicon-edge-npu.html): How we bypassed broken vendor API servers, solved logit collapse with a physical SRAM context-window hack, and built an on-the-fly model hot-swapping daemon.
- [Taming the Edge: Bypassing Axera AX8850 NPU Compiler Constraints](/blog/taming-ax8850-edge-npu.html): A technical deep-dive into reverse-engineering the Pulsar2 compiler, patching PyArmor memory classes in-flight, and executing local LLMs on the Radxa AX-M1 NPU.
- [Benchmarking NextGenRedPVE: Running Local Offensive AI Agents on Proxmox](/blog/benchmarking-nextgenredpve.html): How we tested, why we tested, and what we learned benchmarking local abliterated LLMs for red team operations on our NextGenRedPVE cluster.
- [Reasoning Models vs. Frontier Models in Offensive Security Benchmarking](/blog/reasoning-models-vs-frontier-models-in-offensive-security-benchmarking.html): An in-depth evaluation of local reasoning models versus commercial frontier models, alignment and safety refusal bottlenecks, and agent frameworks like Swarm-AI in offensive security benchmarking.
- [Testing the Gates: Why You Must Emulate Authentication Failures](/blog/testing-authentication-telemetry.html): Why static rule validation fails, and how actively emulating login failures across Windows and Linux reveals hidden gaps in security logging.
- [Demystifying Detection: Emulating Windows Event ID 4625 & SSH Login Failures](/blog/emulating-windows-linux-logon-failures.html): A deep dive into building programmatic triggers for Windows SMB/NTLM and Linux SSH authentication failures to validate SIEM alerts and detection pipelines.
- [Rescuing Abandoned IoT: How I Built JoeBro to Control My Smart Table](/blog/rescuing-abandoned-iot-joebro-sobro.html): When manufacturers abandon their mobile apps, expensive smart hardware turns into a brick. Here is how I reverse-engineered the Ayla Networks API to build a zero-backend PWA.
